the active inference of visual scenes requires a hierarchy of predictive coding, with a posteriori inference (or memory) in ventral visual stream and a priori prediction (or planning) in dorsal visual stream, and that the functional anatomy of visual scene construction is consistent with a normative model of active inference.

the brain is an active inference machine that minimizes variational free energy by sampling the sensory consequences of actions and that this process theory can account for the way people sample information in visual scenes.

active inference can account for the way people forages for information in a visual scene, and that the functional anatomy of the requisite computations can be derived from a normative theory of perception and action.

the functional architecture that underwrites the perception and action of a forager in a visual scene.
the neurobiology of active inference and its implications for understanding visual foraging, the construction of visual scenes, and the role of priors in perception.
the normative and neurobiological foundations of visual foraging and scene construction.

the active inference scheme is a general framework that can be used to study the interplay between the visual system, cognition and behaviour.
